description.narrative: The United Nations Development Program’s (UNDP) ‘’Democracy Strengthening in Zambia (DSZ) project’’ is a three-year multi-donor project designed to address recently identified evolving challenges and builds on previous electoral interventions as Zambia enters its next electoral cycle and the run-up to general elections in 2021

UNDPs ''Democracy Strengthening in Zambia (DSZ) project '' är en treårig insats som stöds av flera givare. Insatsen har utformats för att hantera utmaningar kopplade till de allmänna valen i Zambia 2021 och bygger på erfarenheter från tidigare liknande valinterventioner.

The overall Goal of the project is that Zambia has strengthened democracy through functional and inclusive electoral processes that ensure the peaceful conduct of the 2021 elections and demonstrate heightened legitimacy and institutionalization of the multiparty system. The DSZ consists of two interlinked result areas: (1) electoral institutions and processes strengthened and (2) programming for peace in support of the Zambian electoral cycle. These two result areas are strongly interlinked with following six key results:1. Inclusive and participatory decision-making;2. Strengthened, responsive and accountable institutions;3. Transparent institutions with improved access to information;4. Improved technical and organizational capacities of national electoral stakeholders;5. Credible and legitimate institutions work with integrity, and6. Enhanced conflict prevention and mitigation mechanisms.

The Democracy Strengthening in Zambia (DSZ) project has made substantial contributions to strengthening Zambia's democracy since inception in 2020. The results below are from the period January to December 2023, the additional implementation phase as approved by the Steering Committee in November 2023 and subsequently endorsed by the Under Secretary General for Political and Peace Building Affairs (DPPA). These milestones not only contribute to the ongoing projects results, but also set the foundation upon which further support to the 2026 elections will be built.
The following were some key results attained:
Launch of My e-Parliament Application: an online citizen consultation platform - My e-Parliament - was developed to facilitate regular interaction between Members of Parliament (MPs) and constituents. This was launched by the Speaker of the National Assembly, The Right Honourable Ms. Nelly Mutti, MP on 15 November 2023. The mobile application is accessible on both IOS and Android platforms and provides a user-friendly virtual space for citizens to engage with their MPs and the Parliament at large, with the active involvement of and processing of inquiries by constituency offices. From the launch date to the end of the 2023, the application had garnered more than 1,3 million downloads. It represents a forward-thinking approach to leveraging technology for democratic governance and sets an example for effective parliamentary communication.
Strengthening Electoral Dispute Resolution Mechanisms: The Judiciary initiated a comprehensive review of court rules and procedures for Electoral Dispute Resolution (EDR), drawing insights from experiences in the 2016 and 2021 general elections with support from DSZ. The review centered on key legal frameworks, including the Constitutional Court of Zambia Act No. 8 of 2016, Constitutional Court Rules Statutory Instrument No. 37 of 2016 (as amended by Statutory Instrument No. 29 of 2021), and the Local Government Elections Tribunal Rules S.I. No. 60 of 2016. The culmination of this effort was a review report outlining administrative and legislative recommendations to streamline and enhance EDR processes. This resulted in a comprehensive report outlining proposed amendments to key legislative instruments for further consideration by the parent ministry (Justice). Additionally, using lessons from the region, the Judiciary also established an Advisory Committee on Elections Management. Among other things, the committee is tasked with advising the Chief Justice on matters such as court rules and procedures, institutional arrangements, administrative mechanisms, and effective measures for the expeditious resolution of election-related disputes. Furthermore, the committee is mandated to develop and design a monitoring and evaluation system for overseeing the management and administration of election-related disputes, as well as assessing the performance of courts and tribunals in both pre- and post-election periods. This is a significant step towards institutionalising best practices on EDR.
ECZ Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Policy: The project supported ECZ to develop this policy aimed at integrating principles of gender equality and social inclusion into the operational practices and decision-making processes of the ECZ, extending to electoral operations and engagements with diverse stakeholders. Implementation of the policy has commenced and and will build into the 2026 electoral cycle.
Inter-Agency Working Group on Election Observation Operationalised - The operationalization of the Inter-Agency Working Group (IAWG) on electoral observation missions (EOM) through an official launch by the Minister of Justice, was a significant milestone in the projects support for electoral reforms. The IAWG which is comprised of state and non-state actors, reviewed eight EOM reports from the 2021 elections as follows: EU, Commonwealth, Carter Centre, Africa Union, Christian Churches Monitoring Group (CCMG), Non-Governmental Organisations Coordinating Council (NGOCC), Zambia Federation of Disability Organisations (ZAFOD) and all major electoral monitoring groups. In all, 251 recommendations were reviewed for their feasibility, with 240 either fully or partially adopted for further action. Notably, 11 recommendations were not adopted. The IAWG, recognizing the need for responsive measures, proposed that 162 recommendations be addressed through administrative action, 72 through legislative action, and 10 by policy action. The IAWG's approach, assessing feasibility and identifying responsible institutions, was aimed at ensuring a systematic policy response, work that is expected to continue in 2024 ahead of the 2026 elections.
There are concerns, however, that the IAWG is not progressing as fast as it was intended to.
Disability Inclusion Action Plan Developed. The project supported ECZ on the development of an action plan which encompasses short-term, medium-term, and long-term initiatives, ranging from ensuring the physical accessibility of polling stations to implementing awareness campaigns and leveraging technology for remote voting. This intervention also built on research that was commissioned by the project prior to the 2021 elections, reflecting on the challenges and opportunities for the inclusive participation of PWDs in the electoral process, pursuant to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCPRD). This workshop marked a significant milestone in the ECZ's commitment to creating an electoral environment that is accessible to all citizens, reflecting the values of inclusivity and equal participation in the democratic process.
In addition to the above stated results, the project provides a platform for all state actors in the electoral process to meet regularly through the DSZ technical Committee meetings held every quarter. In this vein, the project has contributed to efficient and coordinated efforts in strengthening democracy in Zambia. It has also given a regular platform for cooperating partners to support the ECZ and other line ministries and agencies through dialogue and sharing of best practices from other countries on an ongoing basis.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
